title: Feral
tagline: The planet's living activity, scored in real time.
proves: Turning a continuous data stream into something with a tempo.
caption: iNaturalist sightings drive a generative score and a WebGPU globe. Real animal field recordings are woven into synth voices; a tfjs sequence model learns the order life is being logged and writes the lead line.

title: Mimic
tagline: Life sorted by sight, not by name.
proves: Clustering by resemblance when the label is the least reliable field.
caption: CLIP embeds every live iNaturalist photo into visual space, and organisms cluster by resemblance, not taxonomy. Where the feed outruns memory, the atlas forgets: hollow expected forms fill the gaps until reality confirms them.

title: Guise
tagline: A camera-led AI transformation study. Guided demo available on request.
proves: Real-time generative video with a person in the loop.
caption: Camera pose locks in, Florence-2 captions what it sees, then FLUX repaints you as viking warrior, marble statue, cyberpunk, or anything you type. Likeness slider, typewriter story beats, and on-demand upscale. Transforms run through a server proxy so the fal key never hits the browser.

title: Forecast
tagline: A machine reading the mood of the species, live.
proves: Putting a live prediction on screen beside how wrong it just was.
caption: GDELT crisis signal drives a WebGPU tension field on the globe. An in-browser LSTM trains on recent volume each session and forecasts the next spike, then narrates headlines as a typewriter voice while the map watches itself get the future slightly wrong.

title: Watcher
tagline: Every person classified. Every scene assessed. Confidently wrong about all of it.
proves: Surfacing a classifier's confidence so its errors are visible, not hidden.
caption: Florence-2 runs in-browser on a grid of live public street cameras worldwide, tracking subjects with templated surveillance dossiers, dwell-escalating threat scores, and a CRT-treated WebGPU HUD. Real VLM inference; the bureaucracy layered on top is fiction.

title: Mirror
tagline: An AI that reconstructs a person from almost nothing.
proves: Showing inference happening, so the viewer can see how little it needs.
caption: Five synthetic characters with procedural WebGPU particle portraits. Browse street scenes, talk by voice, and get replies from an on-device Llama model with audio-reactive lip sync. The surveillance metaphor lives in how confidently thin signal becomes a whole person. Every persona is invented, never a real third party.

title: Latent Atlas
tagline: A museum collection, arranged by what a neural network sees.
proves: Search as navigation: finding by meaning when nobody knows the vocabulary.
caption: 1,500 Met Open Access works embedded with CLIP and laid out in a WebGPU galaxy by UMAP. Fly through visual similarity, then type a phrase and an in-browser text encoder flies the camera to matches by meaning, not tags.

title: Revision
tagline: Every edit to the largest record humanity has ever kept, rippling live.
proves: Making a firehose legible without pretending it is calm.
caption: The global Wikimedia edit firehose drives a real-time WebGPU particle field, where each point of light is a live revision happening right now. Five author archetypes shape the field; the center shows the article being changed this second with edit rate, revert count, and a running narration.

title: Vantage
tagline: The customer-care agent that says the right thing, even when it is thinking something else.
proves: Separating what an agent feels from what it is allowed to say.
caption: A speculative customer-care system exploring the distance between emotional reaction and professional response. Vantage gives Alex a private internal voice, then turns that raw reaction into a calm, useful customer message.

title: Flatten
tagline: A machine that sees in 3D and gets the space wrong.
proves: Designing for a model that is confidently wrong about depth.
caption: Live webcam depth via Depth Anything V2, rebuilt as a broken 3D point cloud. The model's edge hallucinations stretch into visible geometry: smear, confidence, and ghost frames left in on purpose.

title: Amnesiac
tagline: An AI you talk to that loses its memory while you talk to it.
proves: Memory as an interface material: what breaks when context decays.
caption: A local LLM on WebGPU with a corruption buffer that rots conversation history in real time. The model genuinely responds to broken memory: the UI and WebGPU substrate decay as coherence falls.

title: CAPTCHA: After Human
tagline: Ten proofs that you are human, in a world where drawing is the only evidence left.
proves: Designing a test that has to stay humane while it is being adversarial.
caption: Each stage gives you fifteen seconds on a torn drawing surface with a velocity-responsive pencil, then an independent AI answers the same prompt on the right. Both drawings become 3D artifacts: fingerprint contours, a branching organism, a weathered relic. The last stage asks you to redraw your first gesture from memory.
